success.text: "You will? Brilliant. Up the hill. There's a gate made of pallets; you can't miss it." You're in Team Star now, on the inside: the New Kid. Nobody outside knows it.
"Fair enough. Nobody makes you." He folds the card back into his pocket, carefully, as if he'll need it again. Team Star goes on as it was, with you on the outside of it.
The helmet comes off. He's about fifteen. "...Everyone. For a year. Then Star happened. Then nobody."

events.name: Nobody Makes You Talk
events.intro: A hillside. A gate made of pallets. A banner with a star. Tents. Fairy lights, in daylight. A bassline. The gate Grunt, helmet two sizes too big, wrench the wrong way round: "You came! I did the card wrong. I always do the card wrong. Go in. You don't have to say anything. That's rule two." Inside the gate, taped to a post: a field-trip permission slip. On the back, in five handwritings: the Code. 1. Nobody takes your stuff. 2. Nobody makes you talk. 3. You can sit with us. 4. A boss who's beaten steps down. 5. Nobody gets talked out of it.

success.text: You're given a helmet. Atticus made it. It fits. He's never met you. A note inside the band, in tiny stitches: "Spare. For whoever's next. — A." He's made forty-one. He's been keeping one back for eighteen months.

events.name: The Tent
events.intro: A tent. A mixing desk. A sleeping bag. A stack of exercise books to the height of a chair. Odin Fenwright, sixteen, cross-legged, with a protractor: Odin: "You're Fulu. Squad of one. I'm Odin. That's my bag; that's yours; that's the homework." Odin: "I've not been to a class in eighteen months. I've the syllabus memorised. I do the work. All of it. I post it under the staffroom door. Nobody marks it. I got Giacomo to check my maths; he's good. We're not skiving. We just can't be in the building."

success.text: Odin: "You know when you've been somewhere something happened, and your legs won't? It's that. It's not a decision. I get to the gate and my legs won't."
Odin: "I put my name on it. Every sheet. Top right, like you're meant to. I don't know what happens after the door."

Odin: "There was a whole class of us got picked on. Proper. Every day. Teachers knew. We made the team to stand up. We stood up once. All together. Didn't touch anyone. The bullies got frightened and left school. And we got the blame for 'driving students out.' That's the bit nobody'll say."

events.name: Third Period
events.intro: Third period. A bell: it's a saucepan. Twenty kids on crates. Giacomo at the decks, with a whiteboard. Giacomo: "Quadratics. Four-four time. Negative b," (a beat) "plus or minus," (a beat) "root of b-squared minus four a c—" Twenty kids: "—ALL OVER TWO A." Giacomo, to you, not stopping: "Fulu! You're late! That's a detention! We don't have detentions! Sit down!"

success.text: You sit on a crate. You learn the quadratic formula in four-four. Night. The fairy lights. A fire in an oil drum. Odin, in the dark: "You've not said much." Odin: "That's fine. Rule two." A helmet. A sleeping bag. A timetable.

Giacomo: "Nobody's said it isn't! Sit down!" You sit. Night. The fairy lights. A fire in an oil drum. Odin, in the dark: "You've not said much." Odin: "That's fine. Rule two." A helmet. A sleeping bag. A timetable.

Giacomo: "The Academy. We nicked the timetable. It's the same lessons. Same order. Same day. If we ever go back, nobody's behind. That was Cassiopeia's rule. She was dead strict about it." Night. The fairy lights. A fire in an oil drum. Odin, in the dark: "You've not said much." Odin: "That's fine. Rule two." A helmet. A sleeping bag. A timetable.

events.name: The Thing with the Beans
events.intro: Schedar base. A truck on a rise. Somebody on top of it, in very large boots, fixing one. Mela, not looking down: "You're the squad of one. Gate duty. Take the new kid; he needs to see how it's done. Somebody comes, you say 'who goes there,' you battle 'em. That's the job. Don't let 'em talk." The new kid. Yusuf Lightfoot, thirteen, with a helmet under his arm and a shoebox under the other: "I'm Yusuf. I came 'cause my cousin did. He's in Navi. I've been here three weeks." The shoebox has holes in the lid. It's not a Pokémon. It's papier-mâché. Yusuf: "It's nothing. It's a— it's nothing."

success.text: The gate. An hour.

remembers.notice: A line on a rock outside Schedar: BETTER ISN'T FINISHED TILL YOU'VE SOMEWHERE TO GO. Mela: "Yeah. That. That."

events.name: The Gate
events.intro: Then, up the path: a boy in Academy uniform, by himself, carrying a casserole dish with a tea towel over it. The schoolmate: "I'm not here to fight. Yusuf, your mum's asking. She's made the thing with the beans." He holds it out. It's still warm. He's walked it up a hill. Yusuf's looking at his shoes. The schoolmate: "And Mr. Jacq says the science fair's Thursday and there's still a table with your name on. He's not taken the card off."

success.text: He looks at you. He looks at the truck. He doesn't go. He needed to be asked a different question.

Everybody here got— I didn't get it as bad. I came after. I just didn't want to be the one who went back. Like it was fine." A boot, on the truck roof. She's heard all of it. Mela: "Oi. New kid." Yusuf: "...Yeah." Mela: "Is it a good volcano?" Yusuf: "It erupts." Mela: "Then go and do your volcano, kid. Nobody stays here 'cause they've got to. That's not the rule. That's the opposite of the rule." A pause. Mela: "We'll come and watch. Loudly." He goes down the hill with a schoolmate, a shoebox and an empty casserole dish. Mela, to you, lacing the boot: "Don't look at me like that. I'm not soft. He's thirteen."

events.name: Forty-One, One Friday
events.intro: The Academy, at night. A side door. Odin, at the threshold, with his hand on the frame. Odin: "Cassiopeia wants the file. On what happened. Proof. I said I'd go." His legs won't. Odin: "...Give me a second." It takes a minute.

success.text: He goes in. On his own. It's the first time in eighteen months.
You go in. He comes after you, a step behind, the way you'd follow somebody into cold water.
He looks at it. He takes it. You go in together.

events.name: The Corridor
events.intro: Lockers. A noticeboard. EXPULSION NOTICES — FINAL WARNING. Forty names. Odin's is eleventh.

success.text: A cabinet. A drawer by year.

events.name: The Records Room
events.intro: A cabinet. A drawer by year. A folder, eighteen months old. Empty. A sticky note, in a neat hand: "Removed at the Vice-Principal's instruction. See H. — Staff involved reassigned." Odin: "They wiped it. There's no bullying on record. There's just us, with a truck, looking like the problem." One sheet's left, at the back, stuck to the folder's spine. It's the forty-second. "Recommend the group be regarded as the aggressors." Odin: "That's— we told them. Forty-one times. I wrote number fifteen. 'We're not making it up. We compared.' I remember typing it."

success.text: A torch.

events.name: The Torch
events.intro: A light in the doorway. A man of sixty, in a cardigan, with a ring of keys. He hasn't got the wig on. It's the first time. The Director: "...Ah." Odin: "Clive?" The Director: "Clavell. events.name: A Second-Year Who's Scared of the Canteen
events.intro: A phone that rings. Yours. Cassiopeia, a voice changer: "This is Cassiopeia. You've been inside six weeks. You've seen the folder. I'm going to tell you something. I'd like you not to hang up." Cassiopeia: "I founded it. I'm the reason they're out there. I should tell you: I'm also trying to end it. I've been setting people on them. Good trainers. So they'll lose, by their own rules, and go home. It's the only way I can think of to let them stop." Cassiopeia: "There's a bench. By the fountain. I'll be— there'll be someone there."

success.text: A bench. A small figure in a hood.

remembers.notice: Cassiopeia: "You don't fill gaps. That's— I like that. I can't do phones. This is all right."

events.name: The Bench
events.intro: The bench. A small figure in a hood. An Eevee backpack. A laptop, shut. The voice is her own now. Penny, to the fountain: "I got sent abroad when it blew up. My dad's idea. So I wasn't there when they took the blame. I made the plan and I wasn't there. They think I'm some legend. I'm a second-year who's scared of the canteen." Penny: "I wrote rule five. 'Nobody gets talked out of it.' I was so pleased. I thought: no teacher can ever sit us down and be reasonable. And now I can't— I rang Giacomo. A year ago. I said, it's Cassiopeia, you can stop. He said, 'Rule five, boss.' He was proud." Penny: "So I've been hiring people to beat them. That's what I do. I sit behind a pillar and I send strong trainers to make my friends lose. It's the only door I left."

choices.label: "They don't want to stop. They want to come back together."

success.text: Penny: "There's no 'together' to come back to. There's a forty-second report. They'd walk into that building as 'the aggressors.'" A pause. She looks up. First time. Penny: "They— no. They think she's— how long?" "Always. Rule two. Nobody makes you talk." She puts her hood down. Then up again. Then, slowly, down. She gives you a number. It's her real one. You're the One She Meets.

remembers.notice: You could say it: "Eleven hours." Penny: "...Who told you about the ferry." A pause. Penny: "I wrote the timetable rule on the ferry. 'Same lessons, same day, so nobody's behind.' I thought if I couldn't be there I could at least make sure they could come back. It's the only rule I'm proud of."
Penny: "I've read Team Ledger's accounts. They publish. Everything. I've forty-one reports nobody'll admit existed, and there's a gang in Kanto that prints its own receipts."

events.name: As Us
events.intro: A hill between the five bases. An oil-drum fire. Five trucks, parked in a ring, noses out. Five bosses on five bonnets. They don't do this. They've not all been in one place since the shed. Giacomo: "Monday. The notices say Monday. We're expelled by post or we're in the yard." Ortega: "I vote yard. With the engines. Loud. So loud they can't pretend. Star Barrage." Atticus: "And then?" Ortega: "...And then they've heard us." Eri: "They heard us last time. They wrote it down wrong." Mela: "Somebody's got to say it. Do we want to go back?" Nobody answers. The fire. Odin, from the edge, where the squad seconds sit: "If we go back, do we go back as us? With the helmets? Or do we have to pretend it didn't happen? Because I'm not pretending it didn't happen." Giacomo: "Rule five. Nobody's talked out of it." Mela: "Yeah. I know. I know the rule. I'm asking what we want. The rule doesn't say what we want. It just says nobody can change our minds. I'm not sure we ever made them up." The five look at the squad of one. Eri: "Fulu. You've been in the building. You've seen the folder. What's it like in there now?"

success.text: Eri: "...Right." Nobody says anything. The fire.

Atticus: "A box?" "Seventy Fridays. In date order." Giacomo's stopped. Giacomo: "He kept it? All of— my verse-chorus proof of Pythagoras is in a box?" Odin: "He said my quadratics were coming on."

Odin: "A kid in Alola took his trial four times. With forty people watching. I'd take a class with forty people watching."

events.name: How Near
events.intro: Odin walks to the school, evenings. To see how near his legs'll go. You walk with him. The end of the road. He can see the clock.

success.text: Odin: "That's it. That's the record. I can see it."

events.name: How Near
events.intro: Odin walks to the school, evenings. To see how near his legs'll go. You walk with him. The bus shelter opposite.

success.text: Odin: "I used to get off here. I'd my hand on the pole, like this. I can't let go of the pole." He lets go of the pole. He puts his hand back.

events.name: How Near
events.intro: Odin walks to the school, evenings. To see how near his legs'll go. You walk with him. Inside. At night. With a job to do.

success.text: Odin: "It's easier with a reason. I didn't have to be there. I just had to fetch something."

events.name: How Near
events.intro: Odin walks to the school, evenings. To see how near his legs'll go. You walk with him. The gate. In daylight. Break's on; there's noise.

success.text: Odin: "They're playing football. I thought it'd be— I don't know what I thought. It's just football."

events.name: How Near
events.intro: Odin walks to the school, evenings. To see how near his legs'll go. You walk with him. The yard. He stands in it. For a minute. Nobody looks.

success.text: Odin: "Nobody looked. I thought they'd all look." A pause. Odin: "I'm in the yard. Fulu. I'm in the yard."

events.name: Your Lesson
events.intro: A crate. A whiteboard. Twenty kids on the ground. A timetable with a gap in it. Giacomo: "Fourth period's 'Battle Studies.' We've nobody for it. Eri does PE; it's not the same. You've been everywhere. Teach."

success.text: Twenty kids write it down. It's the only lesson they've had on it.
Twenty kids look at their Pokémon. One asks hers something, quietly.

choices.label: "There's others. Like you. They're all right."

success.text: What you did in another region, with people who'd been left out. Twenty kids listen as if it were the news.
Giacomo: "It's on the syllabus. Fair enough."

events.name: Your Lesson
events.intro: A Grunt, hand up: "Is this on the test?" Giacomo: "There's no test. There's never been a test. We've nobody to set one." The Grunt: "...Can we have one? I'd like to know if I'm any good."

success.text: One question. Whatever you like. It's marked the next stage. Everybody passes. Atticus sews a pass-mark onto each sleeve.

events.name: The Seventh Star
events.intro: A hill. No lights. Atticus, with a needle, and a sky. Atticus: "Cassiopeia's five stars. The W. Segin, Ruchbah, Navi, Schedar, Caph. One each. She picked. She said: 'A constellation's just some dots somebody decided went together.'" Atticus: "There's a sixth. Achird. Faint. And a seventh, fainter: Fulu. Nobody uses those. She said to keep them back. For whoever came after." He holds up your helmet. He's sewing something inside the band, where the "spare" note was. Atticus: "I've been unpicking 'spare.' It's taken a week. I do very small stitches."

success.text: He shows it. Seven tiny points. A W, and two more. Atticus: "That's all of us. With you in. And a place for her."
Atticus: "She said: 'There'll be someone who should've been in the room and wasn't. And someone who wasn't in the room and should be.' I didn't understand it. I think the first one's her."
He doesn't answer. He goes on sewing. Very small stitches.

events.name: Voice Changer
events.intro: The phone rings. It's late. Cassiopeia, the voice changer: "Fulu. Report. Segin's morale. Schedar's supplies. Whether Ortega's eating." You report. Cassiopeia: "Good. And— is Mela sleeping? She doesn't. She says she does." A click. The changer's cut out. She hasn't noticed. Penny, her own voice, small, tired: "—because she used to ring me at two in the morning, before. Just to say she was awake. And I'd say, me too. And we'd not say anything else. We'd just both be awake." A silence. She's heard herself. Penny: "...It's off. Isn't it. The thing."

success.text: Penny: "How long?" "Since 'is Mela sleeping.'" Penny: "Oh, no." A pause. Penny: "...It's quite nice. Talking like this. I'd forgotten what I sound like."
She doesn't switch it back on. Neither of you hangs up for a while.

choices.label: "Ring her. At two. Don't say who."

success.text: She does. That night. You aren't on the call. The next day, at Schedar: Mela: "Somebody rang me. Two in the morning. Didn't say a word. Just breathed. I said, 'Me too.'" She's lacing a boot. She's smiling at it. Mela: "I slept after. First time in a year."

events.name: Giacomo, Alone
events.intro: At the decks, headphones round his neck. Giacomo: "I wrote the team song. Nobody's heard the last verse. It's about going back. I can't finish it till I know if we do."

success.text: He does. It stops where the last verse should be. He doesn't fill the gap. Neither do you.
Giacomo: "Nothing. I've checked. That's half the problem."
He picks up a pen. He puts it down. Giacomo: "...I'll write it in pencil."

events.name: Mela, Alone
events.intro: Fixing a boot. Mela: "I was the one who shouted. That day. The bullies ran 'cause I shouted. So if we got blamed, I got us blamed. Nobody's said. I've said it to myself every night."

success.text: Mela: "...Yeah. I did." She goes back to the boot.
Mela: "Maybe." She doesn't believe it. She'd like to.
She's stopped lacing. Mela: "...No. I didn't do it for— no. Nobody has."

events.name: Mela, Alone
events.intro: The boot, half laced.

success.text: She looks at the boot for a long time. She doesn't say anything. She finishes the lace, very carefully.
She finishes the lace.

events.name: Atticus, Alone
events.intro: Sewing. Atticus: "I made every uniform. Forty. By hand. If we disband, what do I do with forty helmets? I'm not being funny. I've nowhere to put them."

success.text: He stops sewing. Atticus: "...It would, wouldn't it."
Atticus: "I've kept one. I've kept one for eighteen months. That's how I know it doesn't help."
Atticus: "Nobody. A book. I sewed under the desk, in lessons. It was the only thing I could do with my hands that nobody could take off me."

remembers.notice: A tea towel in Atticus's tent: ASK THE ONE IT'S ABOUT. Atticus: "Nobody did. Eighteen months. They asked the school."

events.name: Ortega, Alone
events.intro: On a far too expensive chair. Ortega: "My family could've had the bullies expelled in a day. I never told them. I didn't want it bought. I wanted us to do it. And then it went wrong, and I could still buy it right, and I still won't. Is that pride? Giacomo says it's pride."

success.text: Ortega: "...Yeah. Fine. It's pride. I'm keeping it."
He looks at you as if you'd paid him. Ortega: "Tell Giacomo."

choices.label: "Buy the truck a new engine instead."

success.text: Ortega: "I don't buy her engines. I build them. That's the whole point."

events.name: Eri, Alone
events.intro: In the dojo, cooling down. Eri: "I'm the strong one. So I stand at the front. Nobody's asked if I'm frightened. I'm always frightened. I'm just big."

success.text: Eri: "...Yeah. I am. Thanks."
Eri: "Nobody. That's the job." She stretches. She doesn't look at you.
She sits. She doesn't say anything. It's the first time you've seen her sit.

remembers.notice: A lamp at the Caph base gate. Eri: "Somebody posted it from Sinnoh. With a note. 'Ask, and then wait.' I don't know who it's for. I think it's for me."

events.name: Odin Asks
events.intro: There isn't a loyalty test. Team Star doesn't test people. Odin, by the oil drum, not looking at you: Odin: "You've been talking to the Director. I saw. Are you going to tell them, or am I?"

success.text: You tell them. Nobody shouts. Odin, after: "I'm glad you told them. I'd have had to, and I'd have made it sound worse."
He does. He makes it sound worse. They listen anyway. Rule two.
You tell them together. It takes a while. Odin, after: "I'm glad you told them. I'd have had to, and I'd have made it sound worse."

remembers.notice: Yusuf's by the gatehouse. He catches your eye, and nods, very small, as if to say: go on.

events.name: Found Out
events.intro: The gate's shut when you come back. Mela's on it, in her dad's boots, and she won't meet your eye. Mela: "You've been in the building more than we have. With the Director. It's fine. It's not a crime. But it's Monday soon, and we can't have somebody in the tent who's on both sides of the gate." Nobody battles you. Nobody shouts. That's not what they're for. Odin, behind her, holds out his hand for the helmet.

success.text: You give it back. Odin turns it over and puts it under his arm, carefully, like something he'll be asked to look after. You're outside Team Star now. Nobody's angry. That's somehow worse.
